artwork_craft.why: The showstopper cap applies, so this criterion can't go above 6. Frames 4, 6 and 8 fail question 3 outright: none has a sky, a horizon or haze. Frame 6 is a flat brown top-down field of 'F'-shaped mast glyphs on dark pads. The masts stick out past the top edges of their pads, and the 'drive aisle' is just a darker stripe. It reads as an infographic, not a place. Frame 4 is straight down with no hero. The grass scatter reads as confetti stars on an ochre texture, and the 'back step and patio' are flat mauve slabs, where the dossier promised a broom-finish concrete step. On frame 8, the fence 'close behind the table' fills the top 45% as giant planks that splay outward at both edges (wide-angle distortion). The hook sits on the stripes, the cup is a clean untextured cylinder, and the page's Table 2.2-1 has no column headers, so 9,932 / 65 / 1,300 / 65,000 / 195,000 are unlabelled. The frames that do stand in a place still read as CG. Frames 1 and 7 have windowless or black-hole-window box houses. Frames 5 and 7 use capsule mannequins with no face or hands. On frame 5 the bricks are about twice the width of the figure's head, so the wall that should work as a scale ruler breaks the scale instead. The dossier asked for buff block and the render is red brick. Frame 3 has visible posterization contours in the upper-right sky and blotchy mottling across the roof. Per frame: 6, 7, 5.5, 4.5, 5, 3.5, 5, 5.5, 6.5, a mean of 5.39. Frame 2 is the one frame a designer would ask about: a hazy aerial of the block with long shadows and a readable 330 ft leader. Frame 9's into-the-sun open gate is the best idea in the deck, but its sun is a white disc with a soft halo in a flat mauve sky, and the promised rim light on the fence isn't there. The fence is a pure silhouette.

deck_coherence.why: It clearly tries to be one world, and mostly is. The cedar fence recurs on frames 1, 3, 4, 7, 8 and 9. Straw grass and a blue-to-gold dusk sky recur. The cyan line motif really does change state across 1, 2, 3 and 7 and is gone on 9, and the shut-to-open gate pays off. Frame 6 sits completely outside the deck: no sky, no light direction, a flat brown field with no grade, and a 432 px reader sees a different product. Frame 4 is nearly abstract and shares only the fence. The hero isn't held as one object in one material. It's a black X silhouette on frame 2, an off-white capsule on frames 1, 3 and 7, and a long white cigar under a black slab arm on frame 5, and nothing ties those together at feed size. The two people (frames 5 and 7) are different mannequins. That's more than 'one frame slightly outside', so it sits under 7.

claim_integrity.why: Every numeral I checked traces: 330 (c11/c19), 75 (c19), 63/8/7.8/8 (c13, c14), 220/4,400/220,000 and all table cells (c7, verbatim, and the rows sum), 36 (c32), 400/58.1 (c21, c29), 65 (c20), October 11th (c2), and the address (c3). The mast counts per block match 30/30/30/65/65. There are two encoding stretches, neither a hard fail. First, frame 7 draws DNL bars from zero at one linear scale. The 58.1 bar is 89% of the 65 bar, which visually says 'almost at the line' on a log metric, where 7 dB is roughly a fifth of the sound energy. Second, 'FAA TEST APPLIES AT DNL 65 dB AND ABOVE' compresses c20's test, which is a 1.5 dB increase at or into 65. The frame 8 table carries c7's numbers with none of the column meanings the claim's own note records (area in square miles, chargers, dropboxes, deliveries, transits).

story_and_stakes.why: It names the body (FAA), the applicant (Zipline), the five metros, the deadline (October 11th) and the exact action: the email and the subject line on frame 9. The caption also gives a sharp, answerable question for a commenter to ask: will the final say how often an operator is sent an image? No county is named. That's defensible given the rejected county count, but a Texan in Bexar or Harris isn't told they are inside it. The privacy stake of an image of a yard going to an operator is implied, never stated.

sequence_and_momentum.why: Frames 1 to 4 build the mechanism cleanly (hold, lower, judge, escalate). Frames 5 and 6, weight and charger count, are a sideways detour into spec-sheet facts that interrupt the pod thread before the noise and authorship turn. Frame 8 ('Zipline prepared it') is the real turn. The close lands on an actionable ask with the gate open. Frame 5 is the most cuttable frame.

voice.why: It's clean and scrupulously attributed ('the draft says' on frames 4, 7, 8 and 9), with no first person and no colons. It's also flat and procedural. 'Up to 220 Chargers', with the capital C, is the applicant's product vocabulary set as a headline. The caption's 'The deck walks from a back yard to the draft's own pages.' is a machine describing its own structure. Regional specificity stops at 'a Texas yard'.

variety.why: This is the first golden-hour exterior render in the window, and its palette (blue zenith, cedar, straw) is clearly distinct from no. 32's near-black genset yard at a median L* of 6.9. Three moves carry over from no. 32 and earlier: the capsule person at 1.70 m, the parallel-camera count frame, and the document-on-a-surface frame, which is at least the fifth deck in the window to do it. The kicker-top-left, counter-top-right, Fraunces-hook skeleton is unchanged on all nine frames.

one_sentence_fix: Build the recurring set pieces to photographic fidelity in the chassis before any frame is composed: houses with glazed windows, eaves and trim, a proper modelled figure instead of capsules, brick and boards at true scale with grain. Then require every frame, including the count and the document, to keep a sky or horizon band in the declared world, e.g. frame 6 shot from high on a long lens with the golden-hour horizon across its top and frame 8 with the yard and sky beyond the table rather than a wall of planks.
other_findings: Weighted 6.87 is under the 8.0 bar. This refusal is on the number, not a fault. Even setting the showstopper cap aside, this is an acceptable deck with one genuinely good frame (2), not a good deck.
Frame 3 has banding and mottle in the sky and on the roof (visible contour steps in the upper-right sky, blotches across the roof plane). Look at it at full size before calling the world 'graded'.

Frame 7's headline and dek sit on a smeared, noisy brown ground texture below the fence. The type reads, but not in 'quiet the picture made'. The horizon between the houses is an empty plane running into haze, a small void.
Frame 1 cites c19 in its source line, but its dossier's claims list omits c19. That's a harmless plan and render mismatch.
copy.json's note says frame 8's page carries c5 as well as c27, but the render shows only c6, the table and c27.
Frame 9's parcel shadow sits below the box, detached, rather than reading as a contact. There's no dark core where the box meets the grass.
